title: Oliver Bearman questions 'crazy' stewards decision after launching F1 attack
excerpt:
Oliver Bearman has branded the stewards' decision to hand him a 10-second penalty in the United States Grand Prix as "crazy" and "very excessive."

After the early virtual safety car restart, Bearman got a run on Alpine's Pierre Gasly into the Turn 12 braking zone, and was able to position himself for a move up the inside of the following right-hander of Turn 13.

Mounting the kerb, he barged past the French driver, but the stewards immediately placed him under investigation for causing a collision.

Ultimately, Bearman was handed a 10-second penalty for the incident, which involved his front-left tyre clipping the right-hand side of Gasly's car as he made the move stick.

In the end, Bearman was forced to retire with "catastrophic" damage to his Haas machine from the incident, whilst Gasly went on to score one point for a P10 finish.

However, reflecting, Bearman was critical of the stewards' decision to penalise him, given other examples this season, and what he believed to be mitigating factors.

"I was pretty shocked, to be honest. If anything, it was a racing incident. I felt a bit hard done by for it to be a 10-second penalty as well, especially given some of the incidents that have happened this year that have gone either unpenalized or were a five-second penalty," Bearman told media, including RacingNews365.

"10 seconds for that type of incident seems very excessive, in my opinion, given what happened. I had a great start. I had a great first lap. I also had a really good VSC restart to give myself the opportunity to attack on Pierre.

"I went up the inside into Turn 13. I felt like I had enough of my car alongside to justify it and feel like I earned a bit of space, and didn't really get that space. I was climbing up onto the kerb trying to avoid contact, but I simply couldn't.

"I couldn't disappear once I decided to go for the move. I didn't lock up. I didn't lose any control. It was just that I couldn't disappear at that stage. And 10 seconds is crazy given all of those facts.

"So to be honest, the more penalising thing was that I picked up a bit of damage. It was a very small touch, but it loosened basically the floorboard, and that slowly vibrated its way off over the next few laps, and the car was just deteriorating.

"I had maybe five laps where I was actually feeling very good, and everything was fine. And then slowly, step by step, the car was getting worse, and it was game over.

"It was getting dangerous. I mean, the car was very unpredictable, and on top of that, mileage on the engine and all of the parts are important.

"It was very clear that suddenly I went from having a bit of damage on the car to having a catastrophic amount of damage on the car, and I just said: 'I'm not in this race anymore. I'm going to let Esteban go."

title: Alex Albon responds to Fernando Alonso 'back of the grid' driver gibe
excerpt:
Alex Albon insists his fight with Fernando Alonso in the United States GP was "fun" and "fair" after the Aston Martin driver landed a jab at the Williams racer.

On the opening lap, at Turn 11, Albon tried to move up the inside of Alonso at the hairpin before the back straight, but clattered into the side of the two-time champion's machine, destroying the left-hand side bargeboard and aerodynamics.

Alonso would go on to finish in 16th ahead of Albon in 17th, and speaking to the media afterwards, the veteran said that: 'We need to get better and start a bit higher up because I think the bottom of the grid, the quality of the drivers is very low at the moment."

Responding to that, Albon described what had happened in the incident, for which the stewards elected to take no action against him.

"Have you ever watched the Goodwood and see the Mustang and the Mini? Well, it was the same thing as that race," Albon replied to media, including RacingNews365, referencing a clip on YouTube of a more powerful Ford Mustang (Albon) being overtaken by a better chassis in corners [Alonso].

"Well, it was the same thing. It was fun, and it is always fun to race Fernando; he's strong, but he is always fair.

"Maybe he thought I was a bit over the edge, and I don't know; I am sure I'll find out soon enough, but I had a good amount of fun.

"It felt like there was a car on the right side of Fernando, and he gave Fernando enough space as if he thought there was only one car on his inside.

"But then I was on the inside of Fernando, and so it pinched, and I tried to get out of the way on the kerb, but I couldn't.

"So I got damage and was driving around with a broken front wing."

[Article continues below].

Albon's blue flag nightmare

Turning to the rest of his race, Albon explained his hopes of initially being able to finish well clear of the Aston Martins, but he was not able to do so.

"We pitted very early on the final set, and we had a long run on the hards," he said.

"It would have been okay, but when we came out, we were just getting blue flags, so we lost maybe 10 or 12 seconds of race time on the blue flags, and then suddenly I thought Fernando, Lance [Stroll] and team-mate Carlos [Sainz] would not be in my race.

"I knew they were in my race with a few laps to go, so I tried to hold off the Astons because I knew Carlos was on a fresher set, and tried to help him have a chance on the Astons.

"But then in the end, they got through."

title: Lando Norris was 'praying' for intervention for McLaren F1 gamble to succeed
excerpt:
Lando Norris has described how he was "praying" for a late safety car intervention to allow McLaren's strategy gamble to succeed in the United States.

Starting eighth, McLaren elected to run Norris on a one-stop strategy, with the favoured plan for cars around him being a two-stop as he cycled to second place in the closing stages.

On his worn tyres, Norris was being reeled in at great chunks by the two-stopping Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc, who ultimately got past in a double-move at Turn 1, consigning Norris to finishing off the podium.

It then got worse for the Briton, as another two-stopper, Lewis Hamilton, came past, dropping him to fifth as Norris longed for a virtual or full safety car to allow a free stop and change of tyres - something that did not come until it was too late and Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac broke down with five laps to go.

"We tried, and we were not there on pace or anything, so we had to give it a shot," Norris told media, including RacingNews365, of his one-stop attempt.

"If there was any VSC or a safety car, we were right in contention for a good podium, even P2 for a lot of it, so we were hoping, I was praying, but it never came.

"But I feel like it was a good race, the pace was strong, and I feel like I got everything out of it, so I have to be happy, even though a P5 doesn't sound amazing.

"There's not much more we can do.

"The team was debating whether to box onto different tyres or not, and I was hoping to have a better chance with the hard tyre, but it just degraded, so it was more: did we want to box and be safe and box onto another set of tyres, or did we want to stay out?

"We chose to stay out; there was no disagreement, and the team did a very good job on the strategy."

The top five

Liam Lawson - 9.5

Maximised his result in both qualifying and the race, and played the team game by not running in Q3 to ensure Lindblad officially took P9, which would then become P14 on the grid with the penalty, instead of P15. On a weekend the top four teams all finished, ninth was the maximum possible, and he did a fantastic job to finish just 25s behind a works Mercedes - which was the fastest car in race trim - in Antonelli's hands anyway.

Charles Leclerc - 9

Dominant on Friday and made a stunning overtake on the opening lap and put manners on Verstappen into the Esses. Strong charge to come back on his two-stop and steal second place away from the Red Bull. The only blip was qualifying and the sudden track temperature changes, which rocked Ferrari - but he still got ahead of Hamilton on the grid - and made amends by passing both Red Bulls in the first 30 seconds.

Max Verstappen - 9

Was unhappy with Red Bull's strategy, but so nearly rescued second place, only to settle for third. Another strong performance and keeps the momentum building. Made up for his poor first half of the opening lap quickly by the end of it.

Pierre Gasly - 8

Like Lawson, the best Gasly could have hoped for was P10, given the big four teams all finished and Lawson's Racing Bulls was quicker than the Alpine, and kept Lawson honest.

The bottom five

Carlos Sainz - 5

A difficult weekend for Williams - and Sainz gets the assigned par score. Beat his team-mate by a healthy margin in qualifying, but finished behind in the race.

Valtteri Bottas - 5

Nothing overly wrong with his performance, but just as rumours are beginning to swirl about his future, he needs to deliver more than he is showing. 0.080s slower than Perez in qualifying was good, and he was running behind in the race. Has to show more.

Franco Colapinto - 5

The par score for the Alpine driver whose race ended after 35 laps with an engine issue.

Oscar Piastri - 4.5

Eight-tenths slower than Norris in Q1, three-tenths in Q2, and was originally behind in Q3 before Norris got a time deleted for track limits, which put Piastri ahead on the grid. Got told to move out of the way of Norris as he was struggling so much, and then proceeded to finish 22s behind his team-mate on the same strategy - over a pit-stop. Does earn some credit back for keeping Russell behind for so long.

George Russell - 3

Dreadful performance, but the worrying thing is that he does not have any immediate answers about what went so badly wrong and why he is struggling. Was on the pace in Q2, but Antonelli put nearly four-and-a-half tenths on him in Q3. In the race, Antonelli finished 54.3s clear as the title race was all but ended. The penalty was extremely harsh and not deserved, and dropped him behind Piastri - but was unable to pass a McLaren which appeared not to be able to get out of its own way.

title: Toto Wolff declares Kimi Antonelli 'F1 champion' as huge statement made
excerpt:
Toto Wolff believes Kimi Antonelli's commanding performance in the United States Grand Prix was his best yet, as he declared the Italian the new world champion.

Antonelli was faultless in Austin, as he dominated the race on a one-stop strategy to ease to his ninth grand prix win of the season, nearly a minute clear of team-mate George Russell, who laboured to eighth.

The result, coupled with Lewis Hamilton taking fourth, means Antonelli must wait until Mexico to be crowned as the youngest-ever F1 champion, as he holds a 123-point lead over Russell and a 124-point buffer over Hamilton with just 125 left on the board.

It means that if Russell or Hamilton do not win in Mexico, Antonelli wins the title by default, and if either of the Britons win, Antonelli would simply require a ninth place or a 10th place, respectively, to shatter Sebastian Vettel's record from 2010 by over three years.

Reflecting on the dominant performance by the 20-year-old, Wolff felt that Antonelli had delivered a huge statement victory, and that a "tequila party" for his coronation in Mexico City was in the works.

"The main headline is that, for me, it was the best race [Antonelli] has delivered so far, in getting off the start with the inferior tyre and then controlling it at all times," Wolff told media, including RacingNews365.

"The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but he was exceptional, and he outperformed the car.

"Maybe it is a bit harsh to say, but I think his driving style just glues with the car, and we saw that in qualifying, where on his last lap, he could have been another tenth, or a half-a-tenth up.

"It is extremely satisfying to see what he's been able to deliver, and how he is working with the team, with Bono and yielding the results, but it wasn't an easy road.

"I'm happy to say that it is 99.9% done, but he still needs to finish the race in Mexico, so it is either going to be a tequila party, or if it is not a tequila party, then it is going to be in Sao Paulo the weekend afterwards."

[Article continues below].

Wolff explains Antonelli long road

Wolff then offered some insight into the "long road" that has seen Mercedes prepare Antonelli from karting to the cusp of the crown, including the millions spent on his career thus far.

"I wasn't the one responsible for [finding Antonelli]; it was teamwork. It was our junior team run by Gwen [Lagrue] that discovered him when he was 11," Wolff began.

"Credit to that group that have developed him over many years.

"I read an interview with Pierre Ferrari last week, where he said: "What a talent, he reminds me of Niki Lauda.'

"People don't get that this is the work of nine years, the development and hardship of nine years, the integration into the team.

"Working with the engineers and the 10 or more million spent in the development of his career, of his ability, of his character, together with his parents, and it is not that it has just landed like this.

"Many people said last year, after nine races without points, that he shouldn't be at Mercedes, and people in other teams said that he shouldn't be in Formula 1, like with the tears in parc ferme at Spa."

title: Former F1 supplier targeting stunning grand prix comeback
excerpt:
All signs point to Bridgestone entering the fray once again to attempt a return to Formula 1 as tyre supplier, RacingNews365 has learned, with other manufacturers are also eyeing Pirelli’s position.

Bridgestone is actively pushing to return to Formula 1 as a tyre supplier, RacingNews365 understands.

The Japanese manufacturer has kept a low profile, but it was present at several grands prix over the last couple of months, with its involvement becoming far more visible at the last two rounds in Singapore and the United States.

A delegation of high-level Bridgestone experts attended both races, holding background discussions about the company's planned involvement and a possible return to the sport. Bridgestone last supplied F1 at the end of 2010, before Pirelli took over as the championship's exclusive tyre supplier in 2011.

Pirelli's current deal was extended in 2023 to cover the 2025 to 2027 seasons, and the FIA activated a one-year extension option in July 2026. That means the Milan-based manufacturer is locked in as F1's tyre supplier until at least the end of the 2028 campaign.

The contract is awarded through a tender process. The FIA opens the tender, selects a winner, and then makes a proposal to Formula 1 to begin commercial and business negotiations before finalising the deal.

[Article continues below]

© xpb.cc

A Japanese key F1 figure

Sources with insight into the matter, when asked by RacingNews365, give Bridgestone a strong chance of being the next selected manufacturer.

It is understood that the Japanese company is preparing to return to F1 with a technological, business and commercial package that is stronger compared to its previous bid, which was already widely considered to be robust.

During its first spell in F1, Bridgestone competed between 1997 and 2006 in a tyre war with Michelin, before becoming the exclusive supplier in 2007 until its withdrawal four seasons later after the 2010 campaign.

Bridgestone restructured its motorsport division in 2025 and signed a key figure, Hiroshi Imai, to lead the organisation, signalling its F1 intentions.

Imai, re-signed by Bridgestone after a previous spell between 1990 and 2008 before he left to join McLaren, was a member of the company's high-level delegation at the races in Singapore and Austin.

Imai worked at McLaren from 2009 to 2025, serving as chief race engineer, suspension and brakes performance director, and in his final years, director of race engineering. He was highly respected at the Woking team, where his departure was viewed as a significant loss.

Several of RacingNews365's paddock sources have stated that the company's F1 ambitions were behind "luring" back Imai.

However, they also noted that the technological standards are strong enough for F1, as the company is active in numerous high-level racing series.

Bridgestone took over as the exclusive tyre supplier for Formula E for the 2026–27 season, and is present in IndyCar through its Firestone brand. It also competes in Super GT and other series.

[Article continues below]

© xpb.cc

Other suppliers also interested

Although our sources suggest that Bridgestone's bid will be even stronger than last time, a serious battle could unfold for the role of tyre supplier.

The pinnacle of motor racing gives the selected company an unrivalled opportunity to develop and demonstrate its technology level, as well as worldwide premium visibility and an incomparable marketing platform.

It is highly likely that more companies will be interested in the role.

Despite its decade-and-a-half presence, it cannot be ruled out that Pirelli will try to continue. According to our information, other manufacturers are also preparing for the tender.

Hankook's interest has been well known for some time, but there are also rumours that even Michelin might take a shot at the challenge.

title: George Russell seeking Mercedes investigation as title end-game nears
excerpt:
George Russell is intending to "dig deep" into the data with his Mercedes engineers to understand why he was so slow in the United States, as the title race all but ended.

With team-mate Kimi Antonelli scoring a crushing victory, Russell was required to finish at least eighth to extend the fight to Mexico City - which is where he finished following a poor weekend, having failed to overtake McLaren's Oscar Piastri for most of the race.

Russell dropped behind the Australian after a "ridiculous" five-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage on the opening lap, and Antonelli victory and Russell's eighth place mean the Italian now has a 123-point advantage over the Briton.

If Russell does not win in Mexico, Antonelli will be champion by default, with the 20-year-old just requiring a ninth-place finish to be assured of the crown.

Reflecting on the race that all but extinguished his faint hopes of the title, Russell was initially asked about his penalty and whether getting stuck behind Piastri had "compromised" his race.

"The pace wasn't good in the first stint, and when I came out of the pits on the hards, I probably did six laps on the same pace as Kimi, but then I caught up to Oscar, and I just couldn't overtake, so six good laps, 50 bad laps," Russell began to media, including RacingNews365.

"I want to understand why the pace was so bad in the first stint; the penalty was a bit ridiculous, but that was the least of my worries after such a bad weekend."

After a recent breakthrough with his dominant win in Azerbaijan, Russell has once again struggled in recent weeks to match Antonelli's performances, and indicated that he needed time to process the apparent backward steps.

"I don't have the answers right now, and I need to give it 24 hours to think clearly," he added, before going on to express his intention of 'digging deep' with his engineers to try and find a solution on how to extract lap-time from the upgraded W17 machine.

"The window [with the car] is narrow, and we saw in Malaysia, [Antonelli] was quickest in FP3 and then we qualified fourth and eighth, and then this weekend, we were both up there in Q2, and then I was nowhere in Q3 and nowhere in the race," he said.

"He was obviously exceptionally competitive, and there are signs the window is very small.

"I hope that's an explanation for my lack of pace, but I need to dig deep with my team because it is difficult to understand when you are so far off."

[Article continues below]

Russell's end-game approaches

With the endgame nearing in the championship, the fight for second has closed right up, with Russell in second now just nine points ahead of Charles Leclerc in fifth, with Hamilton and Max Verstappen between.

Looking ahead to the rest of the season, Russell declared his sole aim was to help Mercedes win a ninth constructors' crown.

"For me, as long as we win the constructors', that's the main thing," Russell added.

"I'd like to finish as best of the rest, but P2, P3, P5 is not the champion, so it doesn't mean anything."
